title: How Windshield Wipers Work in 60 Seconds 🌧️🚗 #shorts
description:
Windshield wipers were patented by Mary Anderson back in 1903. Today one electric motor drives a worm gear that slows it down and multiplies its force, and a linkage turns that spinning into the back-and-forth sweep of both arms. Rain-sensing wipers shine infrared light into the glass and start wiping when raindrops scatter it away. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#wipers #cars #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Windshield wipers were patented by *Mary Anderson* way back in *1903*.

steps.label: Motor
steps.text: Today a single *electric motor* sits under the hood, spinning fast.

steps.label: Worm gear
steps.text: A *worm gear* slows that spin down and *multiplies the force*.

steps.label: Linkage
steps.text: A crank and *linkage rods* turn the circle into a *back-and-forth* swing.

steps.label: Blades
steps.text: Both arms sweep together, pressing *rubber blades* that squeegee the water off.

steps.label: Rain sensor
steps.text: Rain-sensing wipers shine *infrared light* into the glass. Raindrops *scatter it*, so the wipers start.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Spin, slow, *sweep*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
